text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Thirteen people including six policemen are killed in Likoni, Mombasa in a raid by gangsters in which 30 guns are stolen and property destroyed.
- U.S. Ambassador Prudence Bushnell says the United States will not dictate to Kenyans what kind of constitution or political system they should have.
- A special general meeting of the Kenya Planters Cooperative Union removes three directors and recommends the sacking of Managing Director James Nyagah.
- Thirteen people including six policemen are massacred when about 500 raiders unleash a night of terror at Likoni in Mombasa.
- The European Union urges Kenyan political parties to engage in serious dialogue on the reform process.
- Finance magazine is warned by the high court to stop defaming businessman Kamlesh Pattni.
- Minister in charge of Internal Security Jackson Kalweo vows tough government action against the Likoni killers.
- Kenya and Jordan sign a memorandum of understanding to promote business between the two countries.
- Nairobi Mayor Dick Waweru vows to hold his own annual general meeting despite being voted out of the chairmanship of a powerful committee.
- Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi and Central Bank Governor Micah Cheserem come under pressure from senior ministers to resign of be sacked.
- Employees of Eldoret-based Rift Valley textiles say 75 million shillings are missing from their staff retirement scheme. ($1=60.97 Kenyan Shillings)
